# Bempedoic acid and the statin-intolerant patient

Bempedoic acid is an ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor approved in the United States
in two formulations - alone as Nexletol and combined with ezetimibe as Nexlizet.
The Lipid Association of India's escalation sequence places it alongside PCSK9
inhibitors after ezetimibe, and notes that both ezetimibe and bempedoic acid are
only moderately more expensive than statins, which is what makes them viable at
Indian price points.

Its clinical role is specific and durable: patients who cannot tolerate a statin
at the dose their LDL target requires. That population does not shrink.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

The supplied dataset already contains a bempedoic-acid-plus-ezetimibe entry with
several active players, which indicates the Indian market has moved past
single-supplier launch and into early competitive formation. Spaces caught at
that stage - real growth, several entrants, no entrenched leader - are the
cheapest to enter, because share is still being allocated rather than defended.

The signal reinforces [[S-03]]: both point at the same underlying shift toward
non-statin add-on therapy, and both land on the ezetimibe cluster. The linker
caps their combined contribution so that two sources describing one trend cannot
double-count into an inflated multiplier.
